text:
arjun: Quick follow-up on the soft-window granularity idea for ingress — sharing tradeoffs. TL;DR: leaning toward per-route soft-window + tenant-priority instead of a single global value. thoughts?
marta: +1 for per-route. global felt too blunt for low-latency routes.
sam: curious — if we shrink windows for some routes what happens to hedging costs?
arjun: Good question. proposal today: default 200ms, but allow per-route overrides (50ms for realtime chat, 500ms for bulk embeddings). hedging only triggers after window elapses and only if route flag `hedging: true`. example header we talked about: `x-rw-soft-window-ms: 50`.
lina: I'm worried about doubling work during bursts. more granular windows = more hedges = higher cost on spikes. how do we avoid double-exec on downstream stateful ops?
arjun: Two mitigations: 1) hedging is opt-in per route. 2) hedging is allowed only for idempotent routes or routes with explicit safe-sideeffect annotation. we can also add a max-concurrent-hedges per-tenant. pseudoconfig: ```routes:
- id: chat
  hedging: true
  soft_window_ms: 50
- id: embed
  hedging: false
  soft_window_ms: 500
```
marta: we also need to include soft-window in caching key derivation (cache-prefix) or you'll get wrong hits when route semantics change.
sam: observability needs to expand: per-route metrics for hedges_total, hedges_success, early_cutoffs, degraded_responses. also trace tags: `rw.soft_window_ms` and `rw.hedged=true` so perf dashboards can slice.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for canary-03 on Tue 03:00 UTC :rocket: (automated smoke tests will run)
lina: trailer semantics for partial/early-cutoff responses — proposal: include a trailer `rw-degraded: true` plus `rw-degraded-reason: soft-window` and `retryable: false` when we short-circuit. that helps callers decide fallback.
arjun: agreed on trailer keys. also, for streaming we should emit a `progress` event before cutoff so clients can surface partials (ex: first token timestamp). sample trailer format: ```rw-degraded: true
rw-degraded-reason: soft-window
rw-partial-complete: 0.42```
marta: one more operational thought: we need a SLO guardrail — total hedging-induced token increase per-tenant must be tracked and capped. otherwise a small noisy tenant can explode costs.
sam: +1. we should expose a quota-like hedging budget metric and automatic throttle if budget exceeded.
arjun: I'll update the draft RFC with these items (per-route soft-window, hedging opt-in, cache key rules, trailers, per-tenant hedging budgets, observability). attaching link: https://redwood.example/rfcs/ingress-soft-window (WIP).
marta: great — i'll take the follow-up to formalize the rollout plan and add tests for cache/backpressure. :+1:
